messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Suggested default git merge.ff behavior
parts:
Ben, this question is mainly for you.

We're suggesting turning merge.ff to false:
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Developer-Process#3--preventing-inadvertent-pushes

Is there still a good reason to do this?

The merge bubbles are now causing issues with our submodules. What should we suggest our devs do?




Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Suggested default git merge.ff behavior
parts:
On Friday, November 6, 2015 at 2:55:47 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
Ben, this question is mainly for you.

We're suggesting turning merge.ff to false:
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Developer-Process#3--preventing-inadvertent-pushes

Is there still a good reason to do this?

The merge bubbles are now causing issues with our submodules. What should we suggest our devs do?

I feel like I don't have a good enough understanding of why fast-forward merges are better or worse for submodules than for regular repositories. The wiki should probably recommend git >= 2.0 so that that you push to only one branch by default. I don't really ever push changes into the tree of a submodule; I just change what commit the submodule points to.

Ben

parts: On Fri, Nov 6, 2015 at 4:17 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

And how do you work on math or stan? Is that all done in its own repo?


Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Suggested default git merge.ff behavior
parts:
On Friday, November 6, 2015 at 4:26:45 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
On Fri, Nov 6, 2015 at 4:17 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
I don't really ever push changes into the tree of a submodule; I just change what commit the submodule points to.

How do you do that? (what keystrokes / commands do you use?)

Like if I were doing something in rstan that needed a change in Stan Math, I do

cd StanHeaders/inst/include/mathlib
git branch | grep -F "*" # master
git pull -ff # lots of new branches and commits to branches other than master
git checkout develop # it is currently behind
git pull -ff #  43 files changed, 783 insertions(+), 687 deletions(-)
# do stuff in rstan, run tests, come back to this directory
git checkout master
git log --oneline | head -n 1 # 2060c2d
And how do you work on math or stan? Is that all done in its own repo?

Yeah.  I don't push to the math submodule inside cmdstan or rstan. I only push to github.com/stan-dev/math.

Ben

messages.author: 2c952029259d7788
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Suggested default git merge.ff behavior
parts:
On Fri, Nov 6, 2015 at 8:23 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
On Friday, November 6, 2015 at 4:26:45 PM UTC-5, Daniel Lee wrote:
On Fri, Nov 6, 2015 at 4:17 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
I don't really ever push changes into the tree of a submodule; I just change what commit the submodule points to.

How do you do that? (what keystrokes / commands do you use?)

Like if I were doing something in rstan that needed a change in Stan Math, I do

cd StanHeaders/inst/include/mathlib
git branch | grep -F "*" # master
git symbolic-ref --short HEAD  # nitpick
git pull -ff # lots of new branches and commits to branches other than master
Do you mean "git git pull --rebase" or "git pull --ff-only"?  (Rebase would keep the history cleaner and avoid merge commits when you finally push to the submodule, and --ff is the default.)

git checkout develop # it is currently behind
git pull -ff #  43 files changed, 783 insertions(+), 687 deletions(-)
Same as above.

# do stuff in rstan, run tests, come back to this directory
git checkout master
git log --oneline | head -n 1 # 2060c2d

And how do you work on math or stan? Is that all done in its own repo?

Yeah.  I don't push to the math submodule inside cmdstan or rstan. I only push to github.com/stan-dev/math.

One major nuisance of gitflow is that it can make it difficult to have a nice simple linear commit history in each branch.  I always thought it'd be better to git pull --rebase before merging to the upstream branch to maintain linearity whenever possible... /rant

To update all submodules recursively to master and commit the changes to the outermost git repository, from the outermost one you can do this (git stashes inserted for safety, not necessary if your workdirs are clean):

git stash save --all
git submodule foreach --recursive 'git stash save --all && git pull --rebase master'
git commit -a -m "Updated submodules to upstream master."
git submodule foreach --recursive 'git stash pop'
git stash pop

Also note that you can use "git submodule update --init --rebase --recursive" from the outermost git repo to update all submodules to the revisions in the upstream repository if something was messed up by the above.

It seems like the level of confusion warrants setting up something like Chromium's depot_tools (or Android's "repo" is another option) to manage git superprojects/submodules through DEPS files the way the Chromium project does, rather than through git submodules directly.  (Or even CMake and ExternalProject_Add commands...)

While we're on the subject of dev environments, I know this has been tossed around before, but a Vagrantfile that sets up the dev environment in a VM for anyone wanting to (1) use stan or (2) hack on stan would make the bootstrapping process a lot easier.  You can bundle all this repo management stuff in that Vagrantfile and carry the dev env with you to wherever you go.  This Vagrantfile + vagrantbox can then be uploaded to Hashicorp's ATLAS as the DataScienceToolbox folks did and used as a basebox for any other Stan users (whether Virtualbox, VMware, AWS/EC2, Rackspace, DO, or bare metal)... 

http://datasciencetoolbox.org/ 
https://atlas.hashicorp.com/data-science-toolbox/boxes/dst

And a pony, please.
